chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements [that have been place]d in the Flesh.
chapter_note: This kephalaion is dominated by an impersonal, systematic correspondential teaching layer: the four elements’ pollution-discharge chain (element → bodily secretion → affect → bodily condition) and the mechanism of purification in the body/new man. It is wrapped by a brief hagiographic sitting-scene frame (¶1) and closed by an institutional application contrasting elect vs. sinners (¶9).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic setup (“Once again… the apostle… sitting… He speaks thus”) marks an editorial dialogue-frame, not the teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [ ... ] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [ ... ] and become a danger to the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanism (elements, first struggle, mixture with waste/darkness, stripping garments, pollution lodged in flesh) stays within the cosmic/anthropological system; no institutional address or Gospel overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly structured correspondential chain (element → secretion → passion → bodily state) in an expository voice; classic substrate mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same systematic discharge-mapping; page marker removed per extraction rules.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Further element-to-affect correspondence presented as ‘what things are’ rather than exhortation; consistent with the core chain-logic.

paragraphs.core_text: The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but still in the same enumerative correspondential register (source → emission → named quality). The ‘tree’ is treated as a correspondential term within the system, not an institutional referent.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission of the [tear] is the [ ... ] of these twelve emissions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative enumerative line (“these twelve emissions”) indicates continuation of a numbered mapping set; despite lacunae, the structure is core-style.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] these four elements shall [ ... ] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [ ... ] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological soteriology expressed as process (ingestion of soul-food, purification, establishment in ‘new man’, reception of Light Mind, attainment of rest) without church-institution mapping or citation formulas.

Institutional application anchors purification to the Manichaean social structure (“reach the elect” vs. “sinners”), moving from cosmic mechanics to community categories; thus later pastoral/institutional layer even though ‘transmigration’ language remains cosmological.
